Subject: Subprocessor list and DPA execution timing

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. Attached is an export of our current subprocessor roster (FinPay_Subprocessor_List_v3.xlsx). We have one ask: can Redwood commit to a 30-day notification window for new subprocessors and a documented objection path? - Does Redwood accept DocuSign completion as signature evidence for the DPA?

Appreciate a short checklist we can include in our procurement packet.

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Dec 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Subprocessor list and DPA execution timing

Hi Sanjay — thanks for the list. Short answers up front:
- Yes: DocuSign or AdobeSign signed envelopes are acceptable evidence for DPA execution; we include the signature audit trail PDF in the contract record.
- Notification window: standard is 45 days for major processors, 30 days for low-risk changes; we can offer 30 days for FinPay given the procurement timing, with the standard quiet period exception for emergency security patches.

I've attached a draft 'subprocessor notification playbook' and a sample evidence package checklist (DPA_redlines_finpay_20271212.pdf). Neha, Karthik — can you confirm the objection remediation SLA and whether we can commit to a 30-day statutory notification for this account?

Next steps we propose:
1) Redwood provides the evidence bundle and signed DPA (DocuSign) for FinPay by Fri 12/17.
2) If FinPay raises an objection, we commit to a 15-business-day remediation window and, if unresolved, provide a mitigation plan and temporary contractual remedy (data segregation / additional encryption) for 30 days while both sides agree on a long-term fix.

Kimberly Park
Director, Privacy & Legal Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments: DPA_redlines_finpay_20271212.pdf, DocuSign_Envelope_12345.pdf

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Dec 2027 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Subprocessor list and DPA execution timing

Kim,

We're good on DocuSign evidence. On remediation SLAs: operationally, 15 business days for most objections is doable if the objection is about termination or immediate data access; for configuration or contract redline requests, expect 30 business days depending on cross-team dependencies (infra, eng). For FinPay's case I recommend:
- Agree to 30-day notification for routine additions (as Kim suggested).
- Commit to 15 business days to provide an interim mitigation (technical isolation, alternative processing agreement) when a high-severity subproc is flagged.

I'll prepare the internal runbook steps and the evidence bundle template. Rishi — please flag any capacity or infra constraints for delivering the mitigation within 15 biz days.

— Neha

Attachment stub: internal_runbook_subproc_response.md

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Dec 2027 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Subprocessor list and DPA execution timing

Neha,

15 business days for an interim mitigation is tight but achievable for most vendors. Two caveats:
- If the mitigation requires tenant-level data migration or reprovisioning across clusters, lead time could slip to 25-30 business days.
- We can pre-approve a set of standard mitigations (IP allowlist, per-tenant encryption keys, temporary routing to a dedicated pool) to accelerate response.

I'll work with Infra to add these to the fast-track playbook. Also advise the sales/solutions team to flag any customers using on-prem or private deployments — those may require a different timeline.

Rishi

Attachment: mitigation_option_grid.pdf (stub)
